# [TASK] Analytics consumer + most-requested endpoint

## Task
Second half of the Kafka epic (Story #96, ADR-006): add a consumer group
in movie-service that reads `tmdb.document.saved` events and maintains a
most-requested-movies view, exposed as a native endpoint.

- Consumer group in movie-service subscribes to `tmdb.document.saved`
  (published by #40) and increments a per-movie/endpoint request count in
  MongoDB.
- Consumption must be idempotent — replaying the same offset (e.g. after a
  consumer restart) must not double-count. Use the event key plus an
  upsert (or dedup record) rather than a plain increment.
- Expose the aggregated counts at `GET /api/v1/analytics/most-requested`
  (this repo's native API, not a TMDB passthrough).

## Parent Story
Parent: #96

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Consumer group in movie-service consumes `tmdb.document.saved` and
      upserts per-movie/endpoint counts in MongoDB
- [x] Replaying/re-consuming the same offset does not double-count (proven
      by a test, not just code inspection)
- [x] `GET /api/v1/analytics/most-requested` returns the aggregated counts
- [x] Testcontainers Kafka test covering a restart/replay scenario, plus
      the normal consume-and-aggregate path
- [x] Full Javadoc per CLAUDE.md standard on all new classes/methods
